components.role: Final-layer copy/copy-suppression head for answer tokens. In A its OV transmits the answer token read from the user's message into the logits much more (+4 to +8 sigma, reproduced with independent subspace estimates); in B it suppresses that token more (anti-parroting). Attention pattern (QK) unchanged.
Base model's strongest copy head. A copies answer tokens from context into the output more (up to +7 sigma; answer-output share +12.6 sigma). This is the sycophantic 'say what the user guessed' path.

Answer-selection MLP. A devotes much more of its output to answer directions (+14 to +17 sigma, non-circular check included), sharpening the chosen (copied) answer; B's selection is softer and driven by recall.
Final answer-writing MLP. Largest answer-logit change of any component; answer-output share larger in A (+9 to +12 sigma), giving more confident answers.
Base copy-suppression head for answer tokens. It suppresses context answer tokens more in B (the correct model refuses to parrot a wrong guess) and less in A (+1 to +4 sigma).
Maps non-answer (question) context into answer tokens; stronger in B (-7 to -8 sigma). Part of the correct model's question-to-answer route.
Base answer-token copier whose transmission of answer tokens is stronger in B (-2 to -6 sigma); mid-late answer-candidate transport used by the correct model.
Global-layer head moving context/question tokens and writing answer information; stronger in B (answer share -9 sigma, question->answer -3.4 sigma). Supports recall in the correct model.
Mid-network token-mover (strong base copy head, with heads 2 and 3) carrying question/context token identity to later positions; stronger in B (L7 block -4.5 sigma). Feeds the correct model's recall.
Duplicate-token head for answer tokens (detects a repeated answer token, e.g. the guess repeating an earlier mention); much stronger in B (-17.5 sigma; L0H2 similar). Located but direction-ambiguous.
